steps.description:
We have point $M$ on $\overline{AC}$ with two special properties: it's the **midpoint** (so it cuts $\overline{AC}$ into two equal halves), and $\overline{BM}$ is **perpendicular** to $\overline{AC}$ (creating two right angles). We want to show $\triangle ABM \cong \triangle CBM$.

The key insight: the two triangles share side $\overline{BM}$, have equal legs from the midpoint, and both have a right angle. That's the **SAS pattern** (Side-Angle-Side) — two sides and the angle *between* them match up. We just need to identify those three matching pieces.
steps.title: Understand the Setup

steps.description:
By definition, a **midpoint** divides a segment into two congruent halves. Since $M$ is the midpoint of $\overline{AC}$:
$$AM = MC$$
This is our **first pair of equal sides**.
steps.title: First Side: Midpoint gives $AM = MC$

steps.description:
Because $\overline{BM} \perp \overline{AC}$, it creates right angles on **both sides** of $M$. That means:
$$\angle BMA = 90° \quad \text{and} \quad \angle BMC = 90°$$
So $\angle BMA = \angle BMC$. This is the **included angle** sitting between the two pairs of sides we're matching — exactly what SAS requires.
steps.title: Included Angle: Perpendicular gives two right angles

steps.description:
The segment $\overline{BM}$ is a side of **both** triangles. Any segment is equal to itself — this is the **Reflexive Property**:
$$BM = BM$$
This is our **second pair of equal sides**.
steps.title: Second Side: Shared side $BM = BM$

steps.description:
We now have all three pieces of **SAS** lined up between $\triangle ABM$ and $\triangle CBM$:

| $\triangle ABM$ | $\triangle CBM$ | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| $AM$ | $MC$ | $M$ is the midpoint of $\overline{AC}$ |
| $\angle BMA$ | $\angle BMC$ | $\overline{BM} \perp \overline{AC}$ (both $= 90°$) |
| $BM$ | $BM$ | Reflexive Property |

Two sides and the **included** angle of one triangle equal two sides and the included angle of the other, so by **SAS**:
$$\triangle ABM \cong \triangle CBM \quad \blacksquare$$
steps.title: Conclude: SAS Congruence

| Angle | $\angle BAE$ | $\angle DCE$ | Alternate interior angles, $\overline{AB} \parallel \overline{CD}$ |
| Side | $\overline{AE}$ | $\overline{CE}$ | Given |
| Angle | $\angle AEB$ | $\angle CED$ | Vertical angles |

The two angles are on **either side of the included side** $AE = CE$, so by **ASA** (Angle-Side-Angle):
$$\triangle ABE \cong \triangle CDE \qquad \blacksquare$$
steps.title: Conclude by ASA
